rmt-2008-gen-01.title: The exponent contains a zero
rmt-2008-gen-01.body:
The product $(-6)(-5)(-4)\cdots(2)(3)(4)$ runs through every integer from $-6$ to $4$, including $0$, so it equals $0$. Then $5^0=1$ and the least integer greater than $1$ is $2$.

**Answer: 2**

rmt-2008-gen-03.title: Factor by grouping
rmt-2008-gen-03.body:
$x^3+2x^2-2x-4=x^2(x+2)-2(x+2)=(x+2)(x^2-2)$, with roots $-2,\sqrt2,-\sqrt2$. The only positive root is $\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $\sqrt2$**

rmt-2008-gen-04.title: Pythagorean triples with 11
rmt-2008-gen-04.body:
If $11$ is a leg and $c$ the hypotenuse, $11^2=c^2-b^2=(c-b)(c+b)$, so $c-b=1$ and $c+b=121$, giving $c=61$, $b=60$. $11$ cannot be the hypotenuse, since a prime $\equiv3\pmod4$ is not a sum of two squares. So the triangle is $11,60,61$ and its area is $\frac{11\cdot60}2=330$.

**Answer: 330**

rmt-2008-gen-05.title: Divisibility
rmt-2008-gen-05.body:
$C=\frac59(F-32)$ is an integer (for integer $F$) exactly when $9\mid F-32$. The values $F=32+9k$ between $45$ and $70$ are $50,59,68$. The temperature passes through each exactly once, so there are $3$ such times.

**Answer: 3**

rmt-2008-gen-06.title: Cylinder plus cone
rmt-2008-gen-06.body:
The radius is $\frac18$. The cylinder has volume $\pi\left(\frac18\right)^2\cdot7=\frac{7\pi}{64}$ and the cone has volume $\frac13\pi\left(\frac18\right)^2\cdot1=\frac{\pi}{192}$. Total: $\pi\left(\frac{21}{192}+\frac1{192}\right)=\frac{22\pi}{192}=\frac{11\pi}{96}$.

**Answer: $\frac{11\pi}{96}$ cubic inches**

rmt-2008-gen-07.title: Percentages
rmt-2008-gen-07.body:
$80\%\cdot80\%=64\%$ of all contestants wear both. Of the $70\%$ in tennis shoes, the fraction in jeans is $\frac{64}{70}=\frac{32}{35}$.

**Answer: $\frac{32}{35}$**

rmt-2008-gen-08.title: Track the chance of rock
rmt-2008-gen-08.body:
Let $r_n$ be the probability that move $n$ is rock. Rock is never repeated, and after a non-rock move he plays rock with probability $\frac12$. So $r_{n+1}=\frac12(1-r_n)$ with $r_1=1$: $r_2=0$, $r_3=\frac12$, $r_4=\frac14$, $r_5=\frac38$.

**Answer: $\frac38$**

rmt-2008-gen-09.title: Primes up to 20
rmt-2008-gen-09.body:
$20!=1\cdot2\cdots20$ is divisible exactly by the primes up to $20$ and no others: $2+3+5+7+11+13+17+19=77$.

**Answer: 77**

rmt-2008-gen-10.title: All five before him lose
rmt-2008-gen-10.body:
Player $n$ rolls with $n$ marked faces, so he wins with probability $\frac n6$ and fails with probability $\frac{6-n}6$. Player $6$ wins only if players $1$ through $5$ all fail: $\frac56\cdot\frac46\cdot\frac36\cdot\frac26\cdot\frac16=\frac{120}{7776}=\frac5{324}$.

**Answer: $\frac5{324}$**

rmt-2008-gen-11.title: Recognise a cube
rmt-2008-gen-11.body:
Try $\left(\frac{3+\sqrt7}2\right)^3=\frac{27+27\sqrt7+63+7\sqrt7}8=\frac{90+34\sqrt7}8=\frac{45+17\sqrt7}4$. So the cube root is $\frac{3+\sqrt7}2$.

**Answer: $\frac{3+\sqrt7}2$**

rmt-2008-gen-12.title: Tangents and the inscribed angle
rmt-2008-gen-12.body:
With $O$ the centre, $\angle OAP=\angle OBP=90^\circ$, so $\angle AOB=360^\circ-90^\circ-90^\circ-16^\circ=164^\circ$. The minor arc $AB$ (the one near $P$, on which $C$ lies) is $164^\circ$, so the other arc is $196^\circ$. The inscribed angle $\angle ACB$ intercepts the arc not containing $C$, i.e. $196^\circ$, so $\angle ACB=98^\circ$.

**Answer: $98^\circ$**

rmt-2008-gen-13.title: Prime factorisation of the multinomial
rmt-2008-gen-13.body:
The letters: $I$ appears $7$ times; $S,C,A,L$ three times each; $U,P,E,R,O$ twice each; $F,G,T,X,D$ once. So $N=\frac{34!}{7!\,(3!)^4(2!)^5}$. Using Legendre's formula, the exponents of the primes in $N$ are: $2$: $32-4-4-5=19$; $3$: $15-2-4=9$; $5$: $7-1=6$; $7$: $4-1=3$; $11$: $3$; $13$: $2$; $17$: $2$; $19,23,29,31$: $1$ each. The number of factors is $(19+1)(9+1)(6+1)(3+1)(3+1)(2+1)(2+1)(1+1)^4=20\cdot10\cdot7\cdot4\cdot4\cdot3\cdot3\cdot16=3225600$.

**Answer: 3225600**

rmt-2008-gen-14.title: Enumerate the cases
rmt-2008-gen-14.body:
The couple has $c$ children and these have $c_1,\dots,c_c$ children, summing to $4$. Cases: two children with $2+2$: $\frac12\cdot\frac12\cdot\frac12=\frac18$. Two children with $1+3$ or $3+1$: $2\cdot\frac12\cdot\frac14\cdot\frac14=\frac1{16}$. Three children with $\{1,1,2\}$ in some order ($3$ orders): $3\cdot\frac14\cdot\frac14\cdot\frac14\cdot\frac12=\frac3{128}$. One child alone gives at most $3$ grandchildren, so that case is impossible. Total $\frac18+\frac1{16}+\frac3{128}=\frac{16+8+3}{128}=\frac{27}{128}$.

**Answer: $\frac{27}{128}$**

rmt-2008-gen-15.title: Manhattan distance
rmt-2008-gen-15.body:
Moving only north or east, the raptor's coordinates $x+y$ increase at its speed $15\sqrt2$ m/s (while it moves). You run along the diagonal at $10$ m/s, so after $t$ seconds $x+y=\sqrt2\cdot10t$. The raptor starts at $t=3$, so it has $x+y=15\sqrt2(t-3)$ at time $t$. (A zigzag path can follow your path as closely as needed.) It catches you when $10\sqrt2\,t=15\sqrt2\,(t-3)$, i.e. $10t=15t-45$, $t=9$.

**Answer: 9 seconds**

rmt-2008-gen-15.title: Closing speed
rmt-2008-gen-15.body:
Measure progress along the diagonal: the raptor effectively advances $\frac{15\sqrt2}{\sqrt2}=15$ m/s along it (its path has length $\sqrt2$ times its progress), you advance $10$ m/s. You lead by $30$ m when it starts, and it gains $5$ m/s, so it catches you $6$ s after it starts, i.e. $9$ s after you start.

**Answer: 9 seconds**

rmt-2008-gen-16.title: Rotation permutes H, X, G
rmt-2008-gen-16.body:
A $120^\circ$ rotation about $P$ maps the hexagon to itself, so it maps vertices to vertices cyclically: $H\to X\to G\to H$. Hence $\triangle GHX$ is equilateral with centre $P$ and circumradius $PX=1$. Its side is $\sqrt3$ and its area is $\frac{\sqrt3}4\cdot3=\frac{3\sqrt3}4$.

**Answer: $\frac{3\sqrt3}4$**

rmt-2008-gen-18.title: Hot sauce per day
rmt-2008-gen-18.body:
Eating $3,4,5$ tacos uses $2+3+4=9$, $2+3+4+5=14$, and $2+3+4+5+6=20$ mL. Let $x,y,z$ be the numbers of $3$-, $4$-, $5$-taco days among five, $x+y+z=5$. The bottle is empty after five days iff $9x+14y+20z\ge88$. The solutions are $(0,2,3)$ ($88$), $(0,1,4)$ ($94$), $(0,0,5)$ ($100$) and $(1,0,4)$ ($89$); for example $(0,3,2)$ gives $82$ and $(1,1,3)$ gives $83$, which are too little.

Probabilities (multinomial): $(0,2,3)$: $10\cdot\left(\frac13\right)^2\left(\frac12\right)^3=\frac5{36}$; $(0,1,4)$: $5\cdot\frac13\cdot\frac1{16}=\frac5{48}$; $(0,0,5)$: $\frac1{32}$; $(1,0,4)$: $5\cdot\frac16\cdot\frac1{16}=\frac5{96}$. Sum: $\frac{40+30+9+15}{288}=\frac{94}{288}=\frac{47}{144}$.

**Answer: $\frac{47}{144}$**

rmt-2008-gen-19.title: Backward induction
rmt-2008-gen-19.body:
With two pirates left (3 and 4), pirate 3 needs one of the two votes and his own suffices, so he keeps everything and pirate 4 gets $0$.

With pirates 2, 3, 4: pirate 2 needs $2$ of $3$ votes, so one other vote. Pirate 4 would get $0$ if 2 dies, so $1$ coin buys his vote; pirate 2 keeps $2007$ and offers $(2007,0,1)$.

With all four: pirate 1 needs $2$ of $4$ votes, so one other vote. Pirate 3 would get $0$ if pirate 1 dies, so $1$ coin buys his vote: $(2007,0,1,0)$. The highest-ranking pirate keeps $2007$.

**Answer: 2007**

rmt-2008-gen-20.title: Smallest sum of three squares
rmt-2008-gen-20.body:
The smallest sum of three distinct (positive) squares is $1+4+9=14$, so the answer is at least $14$. And $14=2\cdot7$ is a product of two distinct primes and $14=2+5+7$ is a sum of three distinct primes. So the answer is $14$.

**Answer: 14**

rmt-2008-gen-21.title: Self-similarity
rmt-2008-gen-21.body:
Let $x$ be the value. Then $x=\sqrt{2+x}$, so $x^2-x-2=0$, $(x-2)(x+1)=0$. Since $x>0$, $x=2$.

**Answer: 2**

rmt-2008-gen-22.title: Maximise shared faces
rmt-2008-gen-22.body:
Five cubes have $30$ faces; each face-to-face contact hides two unit squares. Contacts are edges of a graph on $5$ vertices in the cubic lattice. This graph is bipartite, so with $5$ vertices it has at most $6$ edges, and $6$ edges would force $K_{2,3}$, which needs two lattice points with $3$ common neighbours; two lattice points have at most $2$. So there are at most $5$ contacts, achieved by a $2\times2$ block ($4$ contacts) with a fifth cube on top of one of them ($1$ more). Surface area $=30-2\cdot5=20$.

**Answer: 20**

rmt-2008-gen-23.title: Equilateral triangles
rmt-2008-gen-23.body:
You end within $1000$ ft of $B$ iff your endpoint is inside the circle of radius $1000$ about $B$. The two circles of radius $1000$ about $A$ and $B$ meet at $P,P'$ with $\triangle ABP$ and $\triangle ABP'$ equilateral, so $\angle PAB=\angle P'AB=60^\circ$. The good directions are those between $AP$ and $AP'$ through $B$: $120^\circ$ out of $360^\circ$, probability $\frac13$.

**Answer: $\frac13$**

rmt-2008-gen-24.title: Both are centred at the midpoint of the hypotenuse
rmt-2008-gen-24.body:
The hypotenuse is $\sqrt2$ long with midpoint $M$, which is the centre of both semicircles. The circumscribed one passes through the right-angle vertex, so its radius is $\frac{\sqrt2}2$. The inscribed one is tangent to a leg: the distance from $M$ to a leg is half the other leg, $\frac12$. The ratio is $\frac{\sqrt2/2}{1/2}=\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $\sqrt2$**

rmt-2008-gen-25.title: Centres form an equilateral triangle
rmt-2008-gen-25.body:
The centres of the three unit circles form an equilateral triangle of side $2$, whose circumradius is $\frac{2}{\sqrt3}=\frac{2\sqrt3}3$. By symmetry the larger circle has the same centre, and its radius is that circumradius plus the radius $1$ of a small circle: $1+\frac{2\sqrt3}3$.

**Answer: $1+\frac{2\sqrt3}3$**
